references.text: All nations came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, for the famine was severe over all the earth, which explains why Jacob's sons also went there.
Tells of Jacob's family facing famine once again and having to return to Egypt to buy more grain.
Joseph explains to his brothers that there have been two years of famine in the land, and there will be five more years without plowing or harvest.
There was no food in all the region because the famine was very severe.
Stephen refers to Joseph and the famine that brought Jacob's family to Egypt.
Direct narrative follow-up: the grain from the first journey is used up, forcing a new trip.
Describes the outcome of the journey that began in 42:5, showing God's provision through Joseph.
Describes Joseph's response to the famine that also drove Israel's sons to Egypt.
Summarizes the same group that went to Egypt because of the famine.
